sections.overview: Asthenosoma ijimai is a tropical echinothuriid sea urchin, notable for its soft, flexible test and conspicuous venomous spines.
sections.identification: The flattened animal may reach about 13 centimetres across; a dark reddish upper surface, pale spine bands and white spine tips distinguish it.
sections.habitat: It lives on the seabed in the western Pacific, from Japanese waters south toward the Philippines and South China Sea, across reported depth ranges of roughly 7–300 metres.
sections.diet: Species-specific feeding observations are sparse in the references consulted, so a more precise account of its natural food remains uncertain.
sections.behavior: An older Japanese encyclopedia account says it hides in hollows or beneath stones, then returns to shelter after emerging to feed.
sections.reproduction: Laboratory work found unusually large, floating eggs and a lecithotrophic larval development; larvae remain near the surface before settling after several weeks.
sections.ecology: It is a benthic urchin documented across a broad tropical western Pacific depth range, while variation among Japanese populations has prompted taxonomic study.
sections.conservation: No global Red List assessment was located in the databases consulted, and available sources do not establish population trends or a species-specific conservation status.
